subject: Mosaic Labs renewal: term adjustment & capacity runway — kickoff and QBR slot request
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gardner <alex.gardner@mosaiclabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@mosaiclabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mosaic Labs renewal: term adjustment & capacity runway — kickoff and QBR slot request

Hi Alex / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — excited to kick off the renewal and growth plan with Mosaic Labs. Per our call, you mentioned potentially moving from a 12-month to an 18-month term and adding reserved capacity for peak traffic. To get momentum, propose the following kickoff / timeline: 

- Week 0 (this week): confirm stakeholders, high-level uplift (reserved GPUs), and primary commercial ask
- Week 1: mutual action plan + draft SOW + preliminary pricing for 18mo commit and reserved capacity
- Week 2: QBR + technical runbook review (capacity, burst policies, SSO/Security requirements)
- Week 3: finalize commercial terms and procurement paperwork

Can you confirm who from Mosaic will own procurement and legal? Also please share 1–2 preferred time slots for a 60-minute kickoff / QBR next week (we have these options: Thu 2028-07-21 10:00 AM PT or Fri 2028-07-22 2:00 PM PT).

Attached: Mosaic_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (stub) and SOW-draft-v1.pdf (stub) — these are working drafts; we'll iterate once we have the capacity and term decided.

Primary asks for Mosaic: please confirm 
- target term (12 vs 18 months)
- expected steady-state GPU needs and expected burst multiplier
- any procurement lead time or PO requirements
Thanks,
Logan Wright
Strategic Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Alex Gardner <alex.gardner@mosaiclabs.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@mosaiclabs.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mosaic Labs renewal: term adjustment & capacity runway — kickoff and QBR slot request

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear next steps. A few notes from our side: 

- Mosaic is leaning toward 18 months if we can get a predictable uplift rate for reserved GPUs (we currently need 4 reserved GPUs steady-state with the ability to burst to 8 during large batch jobs).
- Procurement is on this thread (procurement@mosaiclabs.com) and will need preliminary commercial terms and an indication of any SOC 2 / Private deployment options. We run SSO via Okta and would prefer to keep data within our VPC for sensitive workloads.

We can do the QBR on Fri 2028-07-22 at 2:00 PM PT — that works best for engineering + procurement. If you can circulate a 60-min invite, include a draft agenda: kickoff, pricing walk, technical runbook for burst handling, procurement checklist.

Also: can you provide a ballpark uplift figure (percent or $) for the 18-month committed path vs our current 12-month plan? Procurement will want that ahead of the meeting.

Thanks,
Alex Gardner
Head of Platform Engineering, Mosaic Labs
alex.gardner@mosaiclabs.com
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Gardner <alex.gardner@mosaiclabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@mosaiclabs.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mosaic Labs renewal: term adjustment & capacity runway — kickoff and QBR slot request

Internal note / action items (looping Alex for visibility):

Karthik — can you produce a preliminary commercial sheet by EOD 2028-07-21 that includes: 
- 12-month vs 18-month committed pricing (token & reserved GPU uplift)
- cost for burst capacity (per-hour or per-token options)
- any one-time onboarding or migration credits we should recommend
Jordan — please prepare a short QBR deck (15–20 mins) and a technical appendix covering: 
- how reserved pools and burst policies work in Redwood Dedicated / Private
- SOC 2 evidence points and where Private deployment affects timelines (SSO/Okta integration notes)
- an ops runbook stub for handling sudden burst events (who owns failover, throttles, and fallback model variants)
Alex / Procurement — we'll share the commercial sheet + SOW-draft ahead of Friday's call. If there are procurement forms or PO templates you need completed prior to signature, please drop them in the thread or SharePoint link.
I've attached the most recent SOW draft as a starting point. Karthik, flag any clauses that need standard legal variant language for Mosaic.
Thanks everyone — target is to enter Week 2 QBR with clear pricing and a measurable runbook.
Logan
From: Alex Gardner <alex.gardner@mosaiclabs.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@mosaiclabs.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mosaic Labs renewal: term adjustment & capacity runway — kickoff and QBR slot request

Confirmed — Friday 2028-07-22 at 2:00 PM PT is good for us. Please send an invite with a suggested agenda. A couple quick asks for the deck: 

- Include an explicit line item for "burst to 8 GPUs" cost and the operational steps for automated scale-up (we want to understand expected latency for scale).
- If you have a short checklist for SOC 2 / Private deployment gaps, please add that as an appendix so procurement can do a quick pre-check.

Looking forward to the QBR. If possible, have the preliminary pricing sheet in the drive by end of day tomorrow so procurement can start internal routing.
—Alex
